regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Grand Targhee is forecast for about 33". Jackson Hole and Big Sky follow. Winter Storm Warning at Grand Targhee from Friday to Saturday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Kirkwood is forecast for about 22". Palisades and Sugar Bowl follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Palisades Monday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Mt. Bachelor is forecast for about 25". Mt. Baker and Crystal Mountain follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Mt. Bachelor Friday and Friday night.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Jay Peak is forecast for about 25". Le Massif and Mont-Sainte-Anne follow. Environment Canada has rain mixed in at Le Massif Friday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Cypress Mountain is forecast for about 20". Whistler follows.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Steamboat is forecast for about 23", 19" of it Saturday. Arapahoe Basin and Vail follow. The NWS is calling for more at Arapahoe Basin: 12 to 21 inches Friday night through Wednesday night. Winter Storm Warning at Steamboat from Friday to Sunday.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Brighton is forecast for about 18", 9" of it Saturday. Alta and Solitude follow.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth is forecast for about 16", 8" of it Tuesday. The NWS is calling for more at Mammoth: 12 to 24 inches Sunday night through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Whitewater is forecast for about 12", 6" of it Monday. Revelstoke and Fernie follow. Environment Canada has rain mixed in at Whitewater Monday.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Sun Peaks is forecast for about 7". Big White and SilverStar follow. Environment Canada has rain mixed in at Big White Monday.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Wolf Creek is forecast for about 6", all of it Wednesday. Taos follows. The NWS is calling for more at Wolf Creek: 6 to 13 inches Tuesday night through Wednesday night.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
